notices.description: This project involves enhancing multiple systems across the Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) department to comply with six legislative initiatives (Intros 195-A, 434-A, 5-A, 6A-, 193-A, and 583-A). The project consolidates the business needs of multiple mandates aimed at improving the efficiency and regulatory compliance of HPD's operations. The mandates are related to the Heat Sensor Program, vacant unit inspections, lead-based paint hazard management, and addressing false certifications of violation corrections. This project addresses specific legislative mandates and operational inefficiencies within HPD.

notices.short_title: FY26-FY28 Bklyn Navy Yard Economic Development Services
notices.description: SBS has determined to enter into a three (3) year contract with the Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation (BNYDC) to provide certain economic development services. The contract term will be from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2028. The corporation shall serve as the Citys representative in connection with all industrial, commercial, waterfront, maritime and any other development projects in the Brooklyn Navy Yard, and shall use its best efforts to assist private developers or governmental or quasi-governmental entities in accomplishing such projects. It is in the best interests of the City to maintain a stable working relationship with BNYDC to ensure continuity of services that were determined reasonably fair in price and approved by OMB. This contract is procured via the sole source method as per PPB Rule section 3-05(b)(1).  LL63 ID # FY26NSBS3
notices.plain: The Department of Small Business Services awarded the Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corp. a three-year, $586,840,920 sole-source contract to provide economic development services in the Brooklyn Navy Yard for July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2028.

notices.short_title: NOTICE OF RATIFICATION OF A MINOR RULES VIOLATION
notices.description:
On October 14, 2026, pursuant to Section 1-02(h)(1)(ii) of the New York City Procurement Policy Board Rules (PPB Rules), the City Chief Procurement Officer (CCPO) ratified a Minor Rules Violation request submitted by the New York City Department of Citywide Administrative in connection with a Competitive Sealed Bid solicitation for Rollers, Asphalt DOT, EPIN 85726B0029002.

The minor rules violation occurred when the Agency failed to notify the two lowest bidders of its determination that their bids were non-responsive within the two-day period required under Section 2-07 of the PPB Rules. This oversight did not affect the evaluation of bids, compromise the integrity of the procurement process, or alter the determination to award the contract to the next lowest responsive and responsible bidder. Upon identifying the violation, the Agency notified the affected bidders and proceeded with the award in accordance with the PPB Rules.
notices.plain: On Oct. 14, 2026, the city's chief procurement officer approved a request from the Department of Citywide Administrative Services that acknowledged the agency missed a two-day deadline to notify two low bidders that their bids were non-responsive for a contract to buy asphalt rollers, and the award went ahead to the next qualified bidder.
